events.title: Octavian Becomes Augustus
events.description: The Roman Senate bestowed the title "Augustus" on Octavian, Julius Caesar's adopted heir. The honor set him apart from every other Roman politician and gave him unmatched prestige.
events.significance: The date is traditionally seen as the symbolic end of the Roman Republic and the start of the Roman Empire. Augustus became its first emperor.

events.title: Prohibition Becomes Part of the U.S. Constitution
events.description: Nebraska became the 36th state to ratify the Eighteenth Amendment. That gave the amendment the three-fourths majority it needed. It banned the manufacture, sale and transport of intoxicating liquors in the United States.
events.significance: Nationwide Prohibition began a year later and reshaped American society. It fueled organized crime and speakeasies. It was repealed in 1933, and it remains a famous example of a constitutional reform that backfired.

events.title: The Shah of Iran Leaves the Country
events.description: Amid mass protests and growing unrest, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi left Iran, ostensibly for a short vacation. He never returned.
events.significance: His departure was a turning point in the Iranian Revolution. It ended Iran's monarchy and led to the founding of the Islamic Republic. The change reshaped the politics of the Middle East.

events.title: Space Shuttle Columbia Launches on Its Final Mission
events.description: Columbia lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on mission STS-107, a 16-day science flight. It was the shuttle's 28th mission.
events.significance: Foam debris struck the shuttle's wing during launch. Columbia broke apart on re-entry on February 1, killing all seven astronauts. The loss led to major safety reforms in NASA's shuttle program.
